By: Tarryn Crossman | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Dancing into the third chapter of life

Further information:
Behind the decks her grey hair is backlit by the green laser lights, she shouts to the ground, and they go wild. They can’t get enough of DJ Joy.

In 2016 Joy’s son died of cancer, his dream was to become a professional DJ, so his mom decided to honor his dream. At 60 years old, she started learning how to DJ. She had an old laptop and some of his old gear. For 3 years, she went to classes and practiced, determined to master this new skill.
Covid hit, and everyone went online, so Joy started releasing mixes via social media, not even sure that anyone was listening, she just kept making music.
But South Africa fell in love with her music and story, and they started dancing. The celeb DJ circuit took notice, and people wanted to see DJ Joy in person, so as soon as COVID regulations lifted Joy started playing real-life gigs, and she hasn’t stopped since.

She has all her gear now, and although she is still DJ’ing for her son, she is also doing it for herself. At a time when her peer group is planning the end of their careers, she is at the beginning of a whole new one, as she opens H20 2022

Through Joy and a specialist, we look at the third chapter of life, a time when conventional careers are ending, where people stop being open to new experiences, and we ask how we keep learning and living passionately over 60.

In Sarah's book, she speaks about this idea of having so much wisdom but learning from people younger than you and what they, in turn, can learn from you, and how this exchange is so lost when these generations don't engage. - I am looking for a celeb DJ to talk to this point. someone that has gigged with Joy and will also be at H20

Script:


5fm
That's right. My babies…live and direct from dance music HQ here in Johannesburg City. If the Roger good show. How are you doing. What a privilege to welcome on to the show. The one and only now legendary, I would say Mama of South Africa's Clubland in the House. Mama Bear, Joy Steffens, Honey Bunny. How doing!

JOY
Roger… Do I love you for that intro? That is beautiful. Thank you so much for having me and me to not.

VO
Joy Steffens hasn't always lived life in the spotlight. She comes from a small town where she worked 9 to 5 while raising her children." Then, her son Dylan was diagnosed with cancer.

JOY
We went to the specialist. I just heard him say, Oh my God, Joy. And then he said, you know, we need to get we need to get Dylan to a hospital. And then I'll just burst into tears.

VO
Dylan's cancer was aggressive, and he was only given a year to live.

MASA
What was the hardest part about watching his health deteriorate.

JOY
Driving him to hospice and having his liver drained because he was in so much pain and then he wouldn't stay over at hospice. He wanted to be at home.

VO
All Dylan ever wanted was to become a deejay. In his final days, he started studying music.

JOY
He had dreams, and one of my friends gave him a beautiful course at Boston College to do music.

VO
But Dylan died before finishing the course, his dream of being a deejay unfulfilled.

JOY
He passed away, you know, right next to me.

VO
Joy was devastated, but chose to honour Dylan's life by finishing what he couldn’t: she enrolled at deejay school.

JOY
When I put my headphones on, my. It takes away the pain comes to the song now. But when you hear that drop comes in, you take this down slowly and words are very important as well. You know, I love to tell a story when I do a DJse…I so you see just quietly. It's just a joy.

UPS MASA enjoying music - music is moving my spirit

MASA
Music's your healer. Yeah.

VO
But its more than just her healer, through radio stations like 5fm playing her mixes and supporting her career Joy’s music has earned her celebrity status in dance music circles.

5FM
Often there's a lot of people that are listening that are going to hear the story for the first time. Do you feel like you're living a dream that he probably would have played out in his life or he might be in the realm that he is? Whatever you might believe by curiously living through you?

JOY
It's crazy, but it's it is just like that. And I think he he's watching me all the time.

VO
But what started as a way to honour her son has become Joy's second chance at life. At a time most are considering retirement - what’s known as Life’s Third Act - she’s embracing a new path.

MASA
How is it weird starting a new career at this stage in your life?

JOY
It was very different for me to do this because obviously, you know, being a 62 year old female and then when people see your gray hair, they're like, oh my gosh, why? How where do you come from?

MASA
On average, we're living around 34 years longer than our great grandparents, yet we're still living by the old analogy of aging being an arch where you grow peak decline, then die. But as specialists around the world steady the third act of life, many are, in fact, finding that maybe our last chapter isn't just about retiring and finding a quiet place to live out our last days.

VO
British writer and life coach Judy Rees is an expert on Life’s Third Act.

JUDY
I'm so delighted to be part of that and to be alive at this point in history when you know, for the first time really we've got more opportunities in better health than we've ever had.

VO
For her book Extra The Art of Growing Older, Judy interviewed hundreds of people in their fifties, sixties and seventies who, instead of planning for the end of their lives, were starting a new adventure.

JUDY
Everything is is is changing, like your waistline, your eyesight, your memories, not so good. So you're very aware that physically things aren't functioning as they were. But it depends in the end what you choose to focus on, because what you focus on is what's going to flourish. There are some amazing examples that we filled our book with case studies, interviewing people who are doing incredible things in their Act three…. You know, the lawyer who retrained as a midwife, the couple who were approaching retirement and decided out of the goodness of their hearts to adopt three small children.

VO
Well into her third act, Joy, a.k.a. deejay Mamabearsteffs, doesn’t let her age define how she lives her life. In October this year, she took to the stage and played the opening set of one of our biggest dance festivals, H2O.

ANNOUNCER
You take the body back. Blah blah

MASA
Would you say that losing Dylan gave you a different perspective on aging?

JOY
Yes! I have got a new zest for life. I have to like remind myself I'm 62..

MASA
Young people love you.

JOY
They all come to me and they call me the spirit animal.

Speaker 6
You look amazing

JOY
Thank you - I had such a good set o my gosh.

VO
Abby Nurock is one of the country’s top deejays. She’s played all over the world with her vinyl only sets.

ABBY NUROCK
Single doesn't care about anyone's attention, thought about confidence and happiness. I think she's an inspiration to all young. She's just like the standard for letting people do exactly what they want to do. You can't not love Joy.

JUDY
One of the things we did was we looked at what people say on their deathbeds, and the key thing was, I wish I'd paid attention to what I really wanted to do in life rather than following everybody else's shoulds and oughts

JOY
Some of us going too much of that, you know, work, come home, cook supper, read a book, watch TV, go to sleep. And I think it's very important that people my age think outside the box, just that doing something that takes you out of that comfort zone.

MASA
Are you scared of aging?

JOY
No. I can feel it in my body that I'm not young anymore. But this loss ignited it for me to carry it on.

JUDY
Nobody gets out of here alive. But I would really challenge you to think about what your own life wants to look like before it's too late. Be brave. Ask yourself some big stretching questions about what you want your life to look like in Act Three and what you're going to need to get there.

JOY
If I had imagined my life at 60, I would never have imagined my journey as it is now.
